questions.q: What share of global energy comes from fossil fuels, according to Smil?
questions.why: Lesson one puts fossil fuels at 75 to 80 percent of energy use, with renewables near 16 percent and nuclear at 4.

questions.q: Which energy source does Smil call reliable and low-emission but badly regarded?
questions.why: The summary says nuclear is reliable and sparing to the planet, yet a few disasters gave it a poor reputation.

questions.q: Which four materials does Smil say the modern world is built on?
questions.why: Lesson two lists concrete, steel, plastic and ammonia, noting that making all four depends heavily on fossil fuels.

questions.q: Why won't solar panels and wind turbines make the world fully green right away?
a: They are built from materials whose production uses fossil fuels
They produce no usable electricity at scale
They cost more than fossil fuels to install
They cannot be recycled at all today
questions.why: The summary points out that even renewable hardware relies on concrete, steel, plastic and ammonia, all fossil-fuel intensive.

questions.q: What does Smil recommend practicing to better understand reality?
a: Thinking in orders of magnitude and powers of ten
Learning to code and analyze data
questions.why: Lesson three says most people cannot grasp a million versus a billion, and suggests using powers of ten and prefixes.
